Stars are self-luminous celestial bodies that produce energy through nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium.

items: Stars generate energy specifically through nuclear fusion (converting Hydrogen to Helium), not nuclear fission.
Ursa Major is frequently cited in exams as the primary example of a constellation (Great Bear).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Stars are self-luminous celestial bodies that create their own light and heat.
Energy in stars is generated by the nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium.
A constellation is a group of stars that forms a recognizable pattern in the sky.
Ursa Major, also known as the Great Bear, is a well-known constellation example.

blocks.content: A constellation is a group of stars forming a recognizable pattern. Example: Ursa Major (Great Bear).
